newsitem.title: UK: EU 96/97 beet crops stage mixed recovery - Czarnikow.
newsitem.headline: EU 96/97 beet crops stage mixed recovery - Czarnikow.

text.p: Sugar beet crops in the European Union (EU) face a mixed outlook, with most but not all producing nations expected to post improved outturns in 1996/97, Czarnikow Sugar said its latest monthly report on Thursday.
"Apart from the further slippage in France, there is a general trend in the EU for crop prospects to improve," Czarnikow said.
It added that provided conditions remained favourable during the harvest itself, there was a strong likelihood that production could approach the level reached last season.
In August, Czarnikow estimated EU 1996/97 sugar output at 16.76 million tonnes raw value after a previous 17.02 million.
France, the EU's largest producer of beet sugar, was one of the areas where the difficulties earlier in the season had not proved open to a late recovery, the report said.
Czarnikow said its initial forecast of 4.58 milion tonnes for final French sugar output appeared optimistic and said the crop would finish more than 200,000 tonnes below this.
"Some marginal areas have benefitted from improved conditions but in the main, assessments of the crop have had to be set further below last year's result," it said.
France produced 4.60 million tonnes of sugar in 1995/96.
But the outlook for other beet producing countries in the EU was better, Czarnikow said.
German sugar production could now reach 4.35 million tonnes this crop year after 4.15 million in 1995/96. In August, Czarnikow forecast 1996/97 production at 4.10 million tonnes.
The German beet crop was staging a good recovery and the final field test result had moved up to second place behind the best level for five years, it said.
"Regional variations in soil types and weather patterns will have produced differing scales of benefit from recent conditions but the overall trend has been one of improving prospects."

Czarnikow also revised upwards its forecast for British beet sugar production but noted that with Britain running a longer campaign than most of the EU, much depended on field conditions for the rest of the harvest.
Czarnikow said British sugar output could exceed the initial forecast of 1.36 million tonnes by some 100,000 tonnes. Britain produced 1.33 million tonnes of sugar in 1995/96.
"The weather in the UK has helped the crop to consolidate the benefits of the September rainfall and field tests have underlined the strong late development," the report said.
"Sunny days and cool nights will assist further sugar build-up in roots which have gained weight over the wet September," it said.

Czarnikow said beet sugar production in Spain could improve by some eight percent over the August forecast of 1.08 million tonnes. Output totalled 1.21 million tonnes in 1995/96. --Jeremy Smith, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8064
